about: Every note line Huragok has written in a host's files, by the thing it was written above: tools/notes_history.py adds a version's. Never take a line out: hosts' files still have it.

|servers_folder: # Huragok: how it runs.
# Huragok is the Engineer: it runs your Project Reclaimer servers from one window.
# Inside it, as in Halo 3: ODST, are the two minds it carried out of New Mombasa:
#   the Superintendent  keeps every server running: backend, [restarts], [watchdog],
#                       [keepalive], and name (what players read when it acts)
#   Vergil              watches over the players: [automod], commands.toml, [relay]
# KEEP IT CLEAN!
# This folder is the root. The other files in it:
#   commands.toml   who's who, and which in-game commands each role can use
#   automod.txt     Vergil's word list (automod)
#   SERVERS/        one folder per server: what `dedicated init` makes (dedicated.toml,
#                   project-reclaimer.exe, game/, data/...). Add a folder, and the server
#                   appears in the window within seconds; remove it once it's stopped.
# commands.toml and automod.txt apply edits within seconds. Edits to this file apply
# when Huragok starts again (the servers keep running meanwhile).
# Check everything without starting anything: start.cmd check (Linux: ./start.sh check)
# Relative paths are from this folder. Windows paths: write them in 'single quotes',
# like 'D:\Servers', or with forward slashes ("D:/Servers"); inside "double quotes" a
# backslash starts an escape (\n is a line break), so "D:\Servers" can't be read.
# Where the server folders are.
|server_folder: # One server folder somewhere else (the folder holding dedicated.toml), on top of the
# ones in servers_folder. ".." is the folder this one sits in (the 0.1 layout).
|dedicated_config: # The name of each server folder's configuration file.
|backend: #   process  the Superintendent: one `dedicated` per server, started and restarted from
#            here, so start.cmd (Linux: ./start.sh) is how your servers start from now
#            on. Windows runs project-reclaimer.exe itself; Linux runs it through wine.
#   docker   the official Docker setup: the Superintendent runs `docker compose` for each
#   command  your own commands, such as systemd units (see [command] below).
#   attach   something else (a startup task, a window you opened). Huragok watches
#            and moderates, but can't restart anything.
|servers: # Which servers, by name as in their dedicated.toml. Empty: every enabled server found.
|name: # The name players read when the Superintendent acts ("restarting…").
|dry_run: # true: record every moderation action as "would have…" without doing it.
|database: # Its records (every player seen, every action with who and why) and its log.
[restarts]: # ── THE SUPERINTENDENT ── keeps every server running ─────────────────────────────
# Players read its warnings with the public notices it posted on New Mombasa's
# signs: "PLEASE REMAIN CALM! Server restarting in 5 minutes: daily restart."
restarts|warn_seconds: # Chat warnings before a planned stop or restart: this many seconds before it, in
# turn ("Server restarting in 5 minutes: daily restart."). Nobody on: no countdown,
# and a countdown ends early once everyone has left.
restarts|after_game_seconds: # A restart "after this game": seconds of notice once the game has ended.
restarts|daily_restart: # Restart every server every day at this local time (24-hour clock), like "04:00".
# Empty: never. One server's own time goes in its [[server]] block below.
restarts|min_uptime_seconds: # A daily restart waits until the server has been up this long.
restarts|backoff_seconds: # A server that died: wait this long before each new start, in turn (the last repeats).
restarts|good_run_seconds: # A server that dies within this long of starting counts as a failed start…
restarts|max_failures: # …and this many failed starts in a row stop the Superintendent trying for now: the window
# shows FAULTED, logs/faulted-<server>.txt says why, and S starts it again at once.
restarts|restarts_per_hour: # More automatic restarts than this in one hour means something is looping: FAULTED.
restarts|faulted_retry_minutes: # FAULTED is a pause, not the end: the Superintendent tries once more after this many
# minutes, in turn (the last repeats: 30 minutes, then every hour), until a run lasts
# good_run_seconds. [] leaves a FAULTED server for you to start (S).
restarts|ready_seconds: # A started server must answer on RCON within this many seconds, or it's a failed start.
restarts|empty_seconds: # A countdown ends once nobody has been on for this many seconds.
watchdog|enabled: # The Superintendent's watchdog. It looks at every server each minute for the cases
# below, and does what each says:
#   "actnow"  restart it right away (players get 30 s of warning, when they can
#   "act"     restart it at the end of the game; right away when no game is on
#   "watch"   only log it and show it in the window
# (Not with backend attach: it can't restart. A server that stops answering at all
watchdog|dead: # Dead: every player dropped at once ("Host roster lost 112 of 112 players"). Seen
# on the live server 38 s after a game ended; it let nobody back in afterwards, and
# the server program's own rule only restarts it after five minutes.
watchdog|no_joins: # Nobody gets in: players keep connecting and none of them joins, while there's
# room. Catches a dead server even when it doesn't say so (2 minutes more are
watchdog|stuck: # Stuck: on the scoreboard after a game with players waiting. When healthy, the
# live server always had its next game running within 2 minutes (109 s at most).
watchdog|slow: # Slow: the server falling behind (its log's "under 54 frames a second") for a good
# share of several minutes. A full server is slow anyway, and a restart doesn't make
# it faster: on the live server's log, restarting for slow frames would have
# restarted it mid-game hundreds of times.
watchdog|memory: # Memory: the server program using more than this many MB.
keepalive|hang_seconds: # A server that has stopped responding: status.json not rewritten (normally every
# 5 seconds) AND RCON silent, both for this long. The game's own supervisor
# waits five minutes without frames before acting.
eventlog|enabled: # Every event as a line of JSON, one file per UTC day: what the server sends.
# Player IPs are in it: keep the folder private.
[automod]: # Dr. Endesha wrote Vergil to watch over his daughter; here it watches over your
# players. Its in-game commands and who may use them are in commands.toml.
automod|enabled: # Vergil acts on the words in automod.txt said in chat, and tells the player why:
# "KEEP IT CLEAN! That isn't allowed here…". Each line there has the words, then
# the kicks, the mutes and the ban its strikes lead to: see docs/automod.md. Mutes
# last through restarts (Vergil mutes them again as they join). A name with a
# listed word in it, or one in names.txt, is kicked as it joins until it changes.
# It starts in dry run: watch the window's VRGL lines (part.automod in
# logs/huragok.log) for what it would do, then set dry_run = false.
relay|enabled: # Vergil's console for moderators elsewhere, through Huragok: the official RCON
# client (or any tool speaking the server's WebSocket console) connects to
# Huragok instead of a server, each moderator with a password and name of their
# own. Their commands go through Huragok's own connection (the 4 console
# spots stay free), only the commands their role allows pass (the same lists as
# commands.toml: a moderator can mute, not ban), players read "kicked by Alice",
# and every command is logged. Each server's console is at its game port plus
# port_offset (49176 -> 50176) for the RCON client and other WebSocket tools, and at
# its game port plus source_port_offset (49176 -> 51176) for Source RCON tools (0
# switches that off). Not encrypted: keep address = "127.0.0.1" and reach it through
# an SSH tunnel or a VPN, as with the server's own console.
[updates]: # One block per moderator. role: moderator, admin or owner. Passwords are 8 to 128
# characters, no two alike (the password is what tells moderators apart).
# password = "a long passphrase only Alice knows"
updates|check: # New versions of Huragok (not the game server), from its GitHub releases.
# It never installs one unless you say so: when one is out, the window says so;
# press U there, or run start.cmd update (Linux: ./start.sh update). Your servers
# keep running while it updates, and only the program is replaced: your settings,
# commands, word list and records stay.
# New versions of Huragok (not the game server), from its GitHub releases. Huragok
# looks when it starts and every check_hours; when one is out, the window's HURAGOK
# line says so until it's installed: press U there, or run start.cmd update (Linux:
# ./start.sh update). Your servers keep running while it updates, and only the
# program is replaced: your settings, commands, word list and records stay, and the
# new version brings them up to date.
updates|install_on_server_restart: # true: install a new version by itself the next time a server restarts.
server_updates|check: # New releases of the server program (Project Reclaimer itself). Players must be on
# exactly the server's version, so a server left behind empties out. Each server's
# auto_update, in its dedicated.toml, is the one switch (D in the window):
#   auto_update = true   the server installs each release itself: it looks when it
#                        starts and hourly, checks the download against the release's
#                        SHA-256 list, and restarts its game at once, mid-game (back in
#                        seconds). Huragok makes sure it did (see fallback).
#   auto_update = false  Huragok tells you: it says so in the window, and when asked
#                        puts the checked program in place of those servers' copies
#                        (the old ones kept in records/previous-program/), each
server_updates|check_hours: # How often Huragok looks at GitHub: hourly, as the servers' own updaters do.
server_updates|install: # For servers with auto_update off. "ask": only say so (press U, or start.cmd update
# --program); "after_game": install by itself and restart each server after its game;
server_updates|follow: # When one server has updated itself, restart the other servers that update
# themselves after their game: they look for releases as they start, so every
# server is on the new version within a game instead of within the hour.
server_updates|fallback: # When a server with auto_update on didn't update itself (its console says the update
# failed, or it is still on an older version 70 minutes after the release came out),
# Huragok downloads and checks the release itself and puts it in place while the
# server is stopped after its game. false: only say so.
workshop_updates|install: # New versions of the Workshop mods the servers list ([workshop] items in each
# dedicated.toml). The server program updates them by itself only once nobody is on a
# server using the mod, which a busy server may never reach; meanwhile players who
# already have the new version can't join. How new versions are installed:
#   "after_game"  when the game ends, the Superintendent stops the server, swaps the
#                 new version in (with SteamCMD, about a minute) and starts it again.
#                 If the fetch fails, the old version is put back. Servers sharing one
#                 content folder are left to the program's own way.
#   "when_empty"  the server's own way: it installs once nobody is on.
# One server can differ: workshop_updates = "off" in its [[server]] block below.
workshop_updates|check_minutes: # Minutes between looks at Steam for new versions (5 at least; 0 leaves each server's
# own setting alone and Huragok doesn't look). Also written into each server's
# [workshop] update_check_minutes, so it downloads the new version during the game.
setup|share: # New servers: the window's N key, or start.cmd new "<name>" (Linux: ./start.sh new).
# Each new server is made with the server program's own `dedicated init`, a package
# from PACKAGES/ (its playlists, game types, maps and Workshop items), a free port and
# an RCON password of its own, then checked with `dedicated check`.
# What new servers take from this folder instead of carrying their own copy:
#   game     Halo 3's files (5.5 GB), once, at game/: linked from a server that has
#            them, or copied from MCC with dedicated init
#   bans     one bans.json: one ban list, one admin list, one VPN allowance list
#   content  one content/ folder (maps, game types, mods, images) for every server. Left
#            out by default: each server keeps its own, so its Workshop mods can be
#            updated after its own games and its custom games stay its own (D gives a
#            server that shares one its own copy: hard links, no space used)
# Every server keeps a ban list of its own (bans.json in its folder): a /ban in game
# is that server's. Huragok keeps its own list of the bans it gives (! commands,
# Vergil) and the admins it makes, and puts them on every server's.
setup|packages_folder: # Your MCC folder, for copying Halo 3's files when no server has them yet. Empty
# means Steam's default folder; leave the line out to link from an existing server.
setup|program: # The server program used for what isn't one server's (making new server folders,
# checking custom games). Empty: the newest copy among the root's and the server
# folders' (by its --version). A command for one server runs that server's own copy.
setup|steamcmd: # SteamCMD, for Workshop items (the window's I key sets this up: finds or installs
# it, signs the account in once, and writes [workshop] into every server folder).
# Empty: looked for in steamcmd/ here, C:\steamcmd, PATH. The account must own MCC;
# an anonymous sign-in can't fetch MCC's Workshop items. Never a password here.
# SteamCMD, for Workshop items and Halo 3's files (the window's I key sets this up:
# finds or installs it, signs the account in once, writes [workshop] into every
# server folder, and gets Halo 3's files). Empty: looked for in steamcmd/ here,
# C:\steamcmd, PATH. The account must own MCC; an anonymous sign-in can't fetch
# MCC's Workshop items or files. Never a password here.
setup|auto_update: # New servers install new Project Reclaimer releases themselves (auto_update = true in
# their dedicated.toml, with a copy of the program of their own). false: Huragok
process|executable: # The server program, in each server's folder.
process|command: # How it's run. Empty: the program itself on Windows, and `wine` + the program on
# Linux, as `dedicated run --config dedicated.toml` in the server's folder. To run it
# another way, give the whole command; {executable}, {config}, {folder} and
# {name} are filled in. Each server's process gets RECLAIMER_DEDICATED_ONLY, so it
process|stop_timeout: # Seconds to wait for a clean stop (Ctrl+Break on Windows, SIGINT on Linux) before
process|stop_servers_on_exit: # false: closing Huragok leaves the servers running, so players aren't
# disturbed, and starting it again picks them up. start.cmd stop stops both.
# true: closing Huragok stops the servers too.
docker|compose_file: # In each server's folder. The server's service name is set in its [[server]] block
# below (service = "server-1"); otherwise server-1, server-2… in order.
[rcon]: # {name}, {slug} (the data folder name), {service}, {port}, {folder} and {config} are filled in.
rcon|use_host_key: # Sign in on the console spot each server keeps for its own machine, so
# moderators keep all 4 normal spots. Needs Huragok on the same machine.
end: # Settings for one server, by name as in its dedicated.toml, when needed. The
# window's T key writes autostart here.
# autostart = true                # started whenever Huragok starts
# daily_restart = "05:00"         # instead of [restarts] daily_restart ("": none for it)
# data = "data/reclaimer-slayer"  # its data folder (from its server folder), when not found by itself
setup|download_game_files: # A server that's missing Halo 3's files (one copied in without the game/ it shared,
# say) gets them by itself: copied from MCC when it's on this PC, otherwise downloaded
# with SteamCMD (about 9.3 GB for multiplayer, 5.8 GB kept). false: nothing is
# downloaded without you; the server waits, and I gets them.
updates|auto_update: # true: a new version installs itself as soon as Huragok finds it, rather than
# waiting for you (the servers keep running; a version that failed to install or
# to start isn't tried again by itself). false: it waits for U.
process|priority: # How much of the processor the servers get before everything else on this PC.
# "high": ahead of everything that runs at normal (browsers, Steam, Huragok).
# "realtime": ahead of Windows' own disk, network and input work too. Windows
# only gives it to a Huragok started as administrator (otherwise: High), and a
# server that runs away with the processor can leave the PC unresponsive.
# for a host who sets it some other way). One server can have its own: D in the
# window, or priority in its [[server]] block below. On Linux these are nice
# values, and above normal needs root or CAP_SYS_NICE.
automod|name_match: # How a word from automod.txt catches a player's name. "anywhere": anywhere in
# it, so hitler catches Hitler, DasHitler and xXhitlerXx; a short word catches
# more than you mean (ass in Classic) unless its line lists -classic. "words":
# only as a word of its own, the name taken apart where its capitals and digits
# change, so hitler catches DasHitler but not dashitler. Either way a listed
# number isn't caught inside a longer one (88 isn't in Mike1988).
automod|across_servers: # Huragok's moderation reaches every server: a mute by a ! command or Vergil
# follows the player to any server they join, a kick keeps them off every server
# until its time is up, and a ban reaches servers with a ban list of their own
# (servers sharing one have it already). The game's own /kick and /ban, and votes,
# stay on their server; Huragok only writes them on the player's record. false:
# Huragok's stay on their server too. Each server's own Vergil is on its page in D.
updates|beta: # true: beta releases too (GitHub pre-releases), to try what's coming before it's
# a full release; a beta can have bugs the full release won't. false: full releases
# only. Turning it off doesn't go back: a beta stays until a full release passes it.

watchdog|mode: # "watch" makes every case watch, to see what it would do
watchdog|report_minutes: # a health line in the log this often; 0: never
watchdog|drop_players: # it counts when at least this many went at once,
watchdog|drop_share: # at least this share of those on,
watchdog|drop_left: # and no more than this many were left
watchdog|no_joins_minutes: # in this many minutes, and none joined
watchdog|slow_share: # a minute is slow when this share of it was,
watchdog|slow_minutes: # and this many minutes were slow
watchdog|slow_window_minutes: # out of the last this many
watchdog|very_slow: # nearly all of every minute, minutes on end:
watchdog|very_slow_minutes: # this many minutes in a row
keepalive|act: # restart it (not with backend attach); false: only report
automod|forget_after_days: # strikes older than this stop counting; 0: never
automod|exempt_roles: # never acted on (roles as in commands.toml; "player" is everyone)
automod|check_names: # kick names with a word from automod.txt in them (names.txt always applies)
automod|cooldown_seconds: # lines this close together count as one strike
automod|split_seconds: # a word split over lines this close together is caught

start: # Vergil's word list (automod): one rule per line, in five parts. KEEP IT CLEAN!
#   words | kicks | mutes | ban | name
# words    The words, separated by commas.
# kicks    How long each kick keeps them out, in order: 30m, 1h, 1d, 2w.
#          The last one repeats. Blank: the server's plain kick.
# mutes    How many strikes come before the mutes (0: muted the first time), then
#          how long each mute lasts, in order: 0, 1d, 3d, 7d. The last one repeats;
#          perm (last only) is muted for good. Blank: never muted.
#          Muted players stay in the game: nobody hears their voice or reads their chat.
# ban      How many strikes come before the ban for good (0: banned the first time).
#          Blank: never banned.
# name     One word players see, and moderators type in !strike. Optional, but
#          name every line whose strikes add up: an unnamed one's are kept under
#          its place in the list (rule2), and move if a line is added above it.
# Each strike is the next step on its line: the kicks, then the mutes, then the ban.
# Examples, and what a player gets each time:
#   rudeword          |          | 0, 1d, 3d, 7d |   | rude
#     1st: muted 1 day   2nd: muted 3 days   3rd and after: muted 7 days
#   worstword         |          |               | 0 | threats
#     1st: banned for good
#   badword, otherword | 1h       | 1, 1d, 7d     | 3 | slurs
#     1st: out 1 hour    2nd: muted 1 day    3rd: muted 7 days    4th: banned for good
#   kickword
#     every time: kicked, never muted or banned
# Mutes last through restarts and follow the player to every server: Vergil mutes
# them again as they join, until the time is up.
# Names: a player whose name has a listed word in it is kicked as they join, every
# time, until they change it; no strike, no ban. Banned names are in names.txt.
# Disguised words (b4dw0rd, b a d w o r d, badwords) are caught without listing them.
# word* also catches longer words that start with it. -word is never caught.
# Edits apply within a few seconds.
# Your rules go below.
#          The last one repeats until the mutes. Blank: the server's plain kick.
#          A time past the start of the mutes kicks, then mutes once they're back.
#   meanword          | 1h, 1d   | 1, 3d         | 4 | insults
#     1st: out 1 hour    2nd: out 1 day, then muted 3 days    3rd and 4th: muted 3 days
#     5th: banned for good
#          perm (last only) is muted for good. Or end with a number alone (no s,
#          m, h, d or w): how many strikes come before muted for good, counted as
#          the ban counts them: 5, 1d, 3d, 7d, 8. Blank: never muted.
#   meanword          |          | 5, 1d, 3d, 7d, 8 | | mean
#     1st to 5th: kicked   6th: muted 1 day   7th: muted 3 days   8th: muted 7 days
#     9th and after: muted for good, never banned
# Names: a player whose name has a listed word in it (anywhere in it, DasHitler for
# hitler; [automod] name_match in settings.toml) is kicked as they join, every
# time, until they change it; no strike, no ban. Other banned names are in names.txt.
# Admins add a word to a line from the game: !banword word slurs; make a new line:
# !banword word | 1h 1d | 2, 1d 7d | 5 | slurs; and take one off: !unbanword word.
# Vergil's banned names: one per line. KEEP IT CLEAN!
# A player who joins with one is kicked, every time, until they change it. There's
# no strike and no ban: the name is what's banned, and a kicked player can come
# straight back with another one.
# Moderators add a player's name from the game with !strike <player> name; admins
# take one off with !unbanname <name>. Capitals, accents, digits for letters,
# spacing and lookalike letters are caught for you, as in automod.txt, and so is
# the name inside a longer one. *name* also catches it inside a word.
# Names with a word from automod.txt in them are kicked too, without being listed here.
# Edits apply within a few seconds.
# Banned names go below.
# Moderators add a player's name from the game with !strike <player> name, admins
# any name with !banname <name>, and admins take one off with !unbanname <name>.
# For a word that's banned in chat too, use automod.txt (!banword): its words keep
# names with them out as well. Capitals, accents, digits for letters,

|prefix: # Who can use which in-game command. Players type them in game chat:
#     !mute Bravo 30m spam
# Everyone in that chat sees the line, and the answer comes back privately.
# Edits apply within a few seconds; if one has a mistake, the log says what and
# the file from before stays in force.
# The roles, each able to use its own commands and those of every role above it:
#   everyone   every player
#   member     the players you list below: regulars, friends, clan. No commands
#              of their own yet; what they get is that no vote can kick them.
#   moderator  the players you list below. The game itself doesn't know about
#              moderators, so what they can do is exactly what you list here.
#   admin      the server's own admins: admins in dedicated.toml, or added in game.
#              They aren't listed here, so there's never a second list to keep in
#              step.
#   owner      the players you list below (you): everything.
# One role each, on a ladder: player, member, moderator, admin, owner. In game,
# !promote <player> moves someone one step up (up to the role below your own) and
# !demote one step down (only someone below you): moderators make members, admins
# make moderators, owners make admins. A ban takes every role away. Each change
# gets a line of its own below, with who they are and who changed it; your own
# comments in the lists stay as you wrote them. Owners change only here.
# Players are listed by player ID, never by name (anyone can use any name). It's
# 64 letters and digits; players find theirs in game under Settings > Online
# services. `start.cmd rcon players` (Linux: ./start.sh rcon players) shows
# everyone's on the server.
# To change who can use a command, move it to another role's list. To switch it
# off, put it in [off]. A command in no list keeps the role it has here. Nobody
# can use a command on someone of their own role or above (owners excepted).
# No vote can kick a member, moderator, admin or owner: Vergil puts everyone
# listed here on each server's vote-kick immune list (the console's `immune`),
# and takes them off again when you take them out of this file.
# make moderators, owners make admins. A !ban takes every role away. Each change
# what commands start with ("/" lines are the game's own)
|cooldown_seconds: # between uses of a command, per player; admins and owners wait for nothing

help: The commands you can use, or how to use one
banname: Ban a name: whoever uses it is kicked as they join, until they change it (names.txt)
demote: One step down the roles: an admin becomes a moderator, a moderator a member, a member a player
kick: Remove them; the server keeps them out 10, 30, 60, then 120 minutes
mute: Nobody hears their voice or reads their chat, e.g. !mute Bravo 30m spam
Nobody hears their voice or reads their chat, e.g. !mute Bravo 30m spam; someone who left is muted as they join
pardon: Let a kicked player back in now
Let a kicked player back in now (a ! kick's: on every server)
players: Who's on, with #numbers and player IDs
Who's on, with #numbers and player IDs; !players nate lists those with nate in their name
promote: One step up the roles: player, member, moderator, admin (up to the role below yours)
roles: Who has which role: owners, admins, moderators, members
strike: Give a strike on an automod rule, e.g. for something said in voice; 'name' bans their name
unmute: Lift a mute, also for someone who left
whois: A player's other names, visits and past actions
A player's record: names, where they are, mutes, kicks, bans and warnings on every server, by ! or / and by whom, and their strikes
ban: Ban their ID, address and device; no time means for good, e.g. !ban Bravo 7d cheating
cancelvote: End the vote under way with no result
endgame: End the game with the scores as they stand
endround: End the round as if its time ran out
load: End this game and load a map and mode
map: Load a map with the current rules
maxping: Show or set the ping limit for joining
mode: Load a mode on the current map
nextmap: Show or pick the next game
pardonplayer: Clear someone's automod strikes and lift what automod did to them
servername: Show or change the server's name until it restarts
teamcount: Show teams, or spread players over this many
unban: Lift a ban with everything linked to it
unbanname: Take a name off the banned names, names.txt
admin: The admins (the server's own list, shared by every server using the ban list): add makes a player one, remove makes them a moderator
The admins (the servers' own lists): add makes a player one on every server, remove makes them a moderator
kicks: Who's been kicked lately (here, or off every server by a ! kick), with who and why; @numbers for !pardon
mutes: Who's muted: Vergil's list (strikes, moderators' mutes) and the server's; @numbers for !unmute
rules: The word list: each line's name, words and what its strikes do
said: The last lines a player typed in chat, on any server (kept 30 days)
banall: Put a ban from this server's list on every server's (a /ban made like a !ban): @number from !bans
bans: The bans in force, newest first, with who and why; @numbers for !unban
banword: Add words to a line of the word list (!banword badword slurs), or make a new line: words | kicks | mutes | ban | name. Names with them are kicked too
changebanword: New steps for a line of the word list: its kicks, mutes and ban, as !banword takes them
restartserver: Restart this server, after the usual countdown for anyone on
toggleglobal: Global voice (V, everyone hears) on or off on this server; with a time (10m, 2h) it switches back once that's up
toggleproxy: Proximity voice (N, players nearby hear) on or off on this server; with a time it switches back once that's up
toggleteam: Team voice (B, teammates hear) on or off on this server; with a time it switches back once that's up
togglevoice: All voice chat off on this server for 10 minutes, then back on by itself; typed again, back on now
unbanword: Take a word off automod.txt (a line left with no words goes too)

start: # Interval messages: said to everyone on every server, again and again, each one
# after its own time. A Discord link, the rules, anything you like.
#   how often | the message
# how often  30s, 10m, 1h, 1d, or put together: 1h30m. Once a minute at most.
# message    As players read it, from [Server]. A long one goes out as a few lines.
# Examples:
#   30m | Join us on Discord: discord.gg/yourserver
#   1h  | Be nice: no slurs, no cheating. Vergil is listening.
# Messages with the same time take turns: two every 30m go out 15 minutes apart, each
# one every 30 minutes. They're only said while someone is on, counting from when
# Huragok first sees the server up.
# Each server folder has an intervalmessages.txt of its own, for messages that are
# only that server's; this one's are said on every server.
# Edits apply within a few seconds. A # starts a note.
# Interval messages go below.
# This server's own interval messages: said to everyone on this server only, again
# and again, each one after its own time. The ones for every server are in the
# intervalmessages.txt in Huragok's folder; this server says those too.

# how often  30s, 10m, 1h, 1d, or put together: 1h30m. Once a minute at most.
